---
title: "Data Analysis in Life Sciences"
---

A five-week introduction to computing for biologists. You will learn what is
inside your data files, how to work in a terminal, and how to use R to turn
biological measurements into figures, statistics and reports that anyone can
re-run. No programming experience is needed.

Start with the [course introduction slides](lectures/00-course-intro/lec.qmd):
why spreadsheets are not enough for biological data.

::: {.callout-note}
All course datasets are simulated teaching data. They are for practising the
workflow, not evidence about real biological effects.
:::

## The five weeks

| Week | Biological question | What you will do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [1 — Files and the terminal](week1/01-files.qmd) | What is in our data files, and where are they? | Tell plain text from Word and Excel files, write paths, use a terminal, unpack and search lab data, meet R |
| [2 — R and reports](week2/06-r-basics.qmd) | How much did the seedlings grow? | Import a table, calculate growth, plot it, and render an R Markdown report |
| [3 — Variation](week3/11-data-quality.qmd) | How much do individual plants differ? | Check data, summarise groups, understand mean, SD, and replicates |
| [4 — Comparisons and lines](week4/16-comparisons.qmd) | Did the treatment work? How do two measurements relate? | Estimate a difference with uncertainty, analyse pairs, fit a calibration line and an association |
| [5 — Bigger data and reproducibility](week5/21-computer.qmd) | Can someone else repeat our analysis? | Estimate how much memory data need, use a remote computer, run a small study, and reproduce and share it |

Each topic in the left menu has **Lecture (slides)**, **Exercises**, and a
**Quiz**. More about outcomes and weekly checkpoints: [About the course](overview.qmd).

## Getting started

- [Windows: install Ubuntu; Mac: open Terminal](intro/ubuntu-windows.qmd).
- [Install R and RStudio, then open your project](intro/r-rstudio.qmd).
- [Download the course project and laboratory archive](downloads/index.qmd).
- [Working on a remote Linux computer](intro/remote-linux.qmd). Connection
  details will be added when the course environment is confirmed.

Then begin with [Day 1: kinds of files](week1/01-files.qmd). Keep the
[terminal reference](reference/terminal.qmd), [R reference](reference/r.qmd),
[statistics reference](reference/statistics.qmd), and
[glossary](reference/glossary.qmd) at hand.
